hook.text: A surgery with a 90% survival rate sounds safe. One with a 10% death rate sounds scary. Same data.

buildup.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed that how information is framed changes the decisions people make.

discovery.text: Frames are mental models that highlight some features and hide others—like a camera angle on reality.

twist.text: We rarely notice the frame. It feels like objective truth, not a chosen perspective.

climax.text: Reframing is power. Changing the frame changes the conclusion without changing a single fact.

punchline.text: The frame shapes the picture more than the facts do.

quiz.question: What is the framing effect?
options: How information is presented changes decisions

details.summary: Framing is how the presentation of information shapes decisions and perceptions. The same information framed differently leads to different choices. A surgery with a 90 percent survival rate sounds better than one with a 10 percent mortality rate, despite being identical.
details.whyItMatters: Framing effects mean that how you present a problem often matters more than the problem itself. Awareness of framing is essential for clear thinking.
takeaways: The same information framed differently leads to different choices
Gains framing and loss framing trigger opposite risk preferences
Awareness of framing effects improves decision quality

faq.question: How does framing affect risk preferences?
faq.answer: Kahneman and Tversky showed that people are risk-averse when options are framed as gains and risk-seeking when framed as losses. A sure gain of $500 is preferred over a 50 percent chance of $1,000. But a sure loss of $500 makes people gamble for a 50 percent chance of losing nothing.

faq.question: How can you detect framing in everyday life?
faq.answer: Restate the problem using different words. If your preference changes, framing was influencing you. Convert percentages to actual numbers. A 1 percent risk sounds small until you realize it means 1 in 100 people. Always ask: how else could this information be presented?
